# Agent's Map

One page for implementing agents and new contributors: where feature logic lives, how it is proven, and where the browser is allowed to matter. Mayon is a two-tier system — data and execution logic behind the repository/storage seams, web UI as a thin passenger on top. The boundary rules are owned by [Architecture Boundaries](seams.qmd); the design rationale is in [Architecture](../explanation/architecture.qmd).

## Where features live

If a feature's logic can live behind the repository/driver boundary without much effort, it must. Decisions and their consequences belong behind the seam (repositories, pure logic modules); pixel/animation behavior stays in the UI.

Some features straddle the DOM and the logic tier — streaming render, expound offsets, selection mapping. The policy splits them: the decisions (what to store, how an offset or selection resolves, what the outcome means) live behind the seam where text tests can prove them; only rendering and animation mechanics stay in components. When a feature touches legacy component-entangled logic, walk that logic behind the seam opportunistically — no mass migration.

Per-seam placement detail: [Architecture Boundaries](seams.qmd).

## How features are proven

The default proving path is text-first, with no browser:

1. Set up an ephemeral test database with `useFileTestDb()` (`src/lib/db/driver/pg-test.ts`).
2. Seed state through the repository seam (`repos` from `#lib/db/index.js`).
3. Call the logic and assert on text outcomes.

The pattern to copy is the chat context assembly test, `src/lib/chat/context.test.ts`. Run with `pnpm test`. This harness is the established testing setup, formalized here as policy — not new tooling.

## Test tiers

Place each test at the lowest tier that can prove its claim; if two tiers can prove it, keep the lower one and delete the higher copy:

- `*.test.ts` — **Tier 1**, `pnpm test:unit`: pure logic, mappers, repositories, and server handlers in Node. No browser, build, or listener. `*.svelte.test.ts` rune-module tests stay here.
- `*.browser.test.ts` — **Tier 2**, `pnpm test:browser`: rendered component behavior in real Chromium. Supply `$app/*` and store dependencies at the module boundary, mock `fetch` with MSW (`tests/mocks/handlers.ts`), and never require the app server, Postgres, or docker compose.
- `tests/e2e/*.spec.ts` — **Tier 3**, `pnpm test:e2e`: only flows needing real streaming, persistence, multi-page navigation, hydration, or auth/setup. Reuse the shared session state, use condition-based assertions, never replay onboarding per test, and block third-party traffic.

`pnpm check:tests` enforces the tier boundaries (`TT-001`–`TT-008`). Every removed or migrated source-text and end-to-end case is recorded with its replacement or retirement rationale in `specs/032-test-suite-tiering/migration-ledger.md`; no test is deleted without a ledger row. Parallelism is capability-gated: more than 2 logical CPUs and at least 8 GiB usable RAM (a GitHub-hosted standard runner qualifies) enables parallel execution, with serial fallback at 2-or-fewer CPUs, under 8 GiB, or unreadable hardware. When no explicit `MAYON_TEST_MAX_WORKERS` cap is set, Vitest chooses its own worker count.

## Where the browser is allowed to matter

The browser covers only what logic cannot reach, at two costs: Tier 2 renders an isolated component in real Chromium, while Tier 3 keeps the few flows that genuinely need the real server, streaming, and persistence.

- UI-only wiring and behavior — the pixel/animation tier the browser is for.
- Visual checks are camera-style (screenshot plus review) and rare. They confirm appearance; they do not double as behavior tests that logic-layer tests already prove. The browser is demoted from courtroom to camera, not eliminated.
- Live-stack verification at RC time goes through the existing doors, `/api/health` and `/api/db/query`. No new runtime surface.

## Enforcement & escape hatches

The boundary is machine-enforced:

- Import-boundary rules in `eslint.config.js`, part of `pnpm lint` — a merge-blocking gate.
- A dependency-direction backstop, `scripts/check-dependency-direction.mjs`, wired into CI (`.github/actions/ci/action.yml`).

A violation fails the gate and names the offending file, the broken rule, and the sanctioned alternative. There are no inline disables: an exception is a file-scoped, justified entry in the escape-hatch block of the enforcement configuration, added through review. When the rules change, they change in the configuration and the seam documents — this page links rather than copies, so the map cannot drift from the rules.
